headline: Record revenue and profit; HPE raises full-year outlook
summary_short: HPE posted record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $10.68B, up 40.0% y/y and 14.8% q/q, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.44 swinging from a $0.82 year-ago loss; the company raised FY26 guidance and introduced an FY27 growth framework.
summary_long: Revenue rose 40.0% y/y to $10.68B, driven by Networking (+148% y/y, Routing adding $775M post-Juniper-acquisition vs $1M a year ago) and Cloud & AI (+22.9% y/y, Server +32.7%). GAAP operating income was $747M (vs a $1,109M loss a year ago that included a $1,361M impairment); non-GAAP diluted EPS reached $0.79. Cash was $5.29B, long-term debt $18.24B; free cash flow was $915M. HPE raised FY26 revenue-growth guidance to 29-33% and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $3.35-3.45, guided Q3 revenue to $11.5-12.1B, introduced an FY27 growth framework (8-12% revenue growth), and completed the H3C divestiture for ~$1.36B cash.

drivers.explanation: Networking revenue rose 148% y/y (Routing added $775M vs $1M a year ago from the Juniper Networks acquisition); Cloud & AI revenue rose 22.9% y/y led by Server (+32.7%).
Management cited operational discipline and executing ahead of schedule on Juniper Networks and Catalyst cost-synergy targets as drivers of the quarter's profitability gain.
Y/y EPS gain reflects higher operating income plus the absence of the $1,361M impairment charge recorded in the year-ago quarter.
HPE raised FY26 revenue-growth guidance to 29-33% and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $3.35-3.45, introduced an FY27 growth framework, and completed the H3C divestiture on May 28 for ~$1.36B cash.
